July 12, 1933.    Morning (Translation)

LABOUR.

Central ChinaDaily News and other local newspapers:

THE MEI KWANG MATCH WORKS.

With reference to the strike on July 10 of
workers of the Mei Kwang Match Works, an American firm,
(formerly the Min Kwang Match Works, a Japanese concern)
at Chow Ka Jao, officers of the General Labour Union
advised the strikers to resume work first and informed them
that the question of the dismissal of workers would be
mediated by the local Tangpu and other political organs.

The advice was followed and the strikers
resumed work at 5 a.m. yesterday. The Police Station
at Chow Ka Jao detailed about 20 policemen to protect
the strikers.

The 10th District Match Workers Union has
sent delegates to make an appeal to the local Tangpu and
other political organs to open negotiations and to report
the resumption of work.

《华中日报》及其他本地报纸：

美光火柴厂。

关于7月10日美商美光火柴厂（前身为日商民光火柴厂，位于周家嘴）工人罢工一事，总工会职员劝告罢工者先复工，并告知他们，关于解雇工人的问题将由当地塘浦及其他政治机关进行调解。

罢工者听从了建议，于昨日凌晨5时复工。周家嘴巡捕房派遣约20名警员保护罢工工人。

第十区火柴业工会已派出代表，向当地塘浦及其他政治机关提出呼吁，要求开启谈判，并报告复工情况。

Morning Translation.

July 11, 1933.

LABOUR.

China Times and other local newspapers:

STRIKE IN THE MEI KWANG MATCH WORKS.

The Mei Kwang Match Works, an American concern,
at Chow Ka Jao employs about 500 hands.
Owing to the frequent oppression of workers by
"Carlson", the President of the Works, and the low rate of
wages, the hands have submitted a joint petition to the
local Tangpu and other political organs and have formed a
10th District Match Workers Union with the approval of the
Gangpu and other political organs.
The management has dismissed Yao Tsen-kuo, an
active member of the Union. On July 9, "Ba Lai Mer", the
Chief Engineer, assaulted workers without cause.
The entire body of workers became dissatisfied
and went on strike as from 8 a.m. yesterday. The strikers
have submitted a petition to the General Labour Union, the
local Tangpu and other political organs asking for assistance.
At a conference held yesterday by the strikers
eleven representatives were appointed to make an appeal this
morning to the General Labour Union, the local Tangpu and
other political organs.

D 3769

劳工事务。

《时报》及其他本地报纸：

美光火柴厂罢工。

位于周家嘴的美商美光火柴厂雇佣工人约500名。由于该厂厂长“Carlson”经常压迫工人，且工资低廉，工人们已向当地塘浦及其他政治机关提交联名请愿书，并在获得岗铺（音译）及其他政治机关批准后，成立了第十区火柴业工会。

资方解雇了工会活跃分子姚振国（Yao Tsen-kuo，音译）。7月9日，总工程师“Ba Lai Mer”（音译）无故殴打工人。
全体工人因此感到不满，并于昨日上午8时起举行罢工。罢工者已向总工会、当地塘浦及其他政治机关提交请愿书，请求援助。
在昨日举行的罢工者会议上，推选出十一名代表，将于今晨向总工会、当地塘浦及其他政治机关提出呼吁。

D 3769

Labour (3)

American Far Eastern Match Factory - transient strike

As a protest against the desmissal of one of their
colleagues for attempting to organize a labour union, the
600 workers of the American Far Eastern Match Factory, an
American concern located at 1971 Kwang Foh Road, Chapei,
declared a strike at 9 a.m. July 10. They resumed this
morning, July 11, on the advice of the 6th District
Chinese Police.

Date November 4, 1932
Subject (in full) Boycott against American Matches.
Made by R.S.I. Duncan Forwarded by Tho Robertson, Supt
Nothing of interest has developed in the matter
of the boycott of matches manufactured by the American
Far Eastern Match Company since my report dated September
13, 1932. Although the boycott is still being felt in
Shanghai there is no sign of it being intensified and
the management of the Match Company believe that in time
it will die out altogether. The cargo of matches which
was held up at Chuanchow is still being detained in
spite of representation by the American Minister to the
Fukien Provincial Authorities.
The American Far Eastern Match Factory, Brenan
Road, is still listed in the Telephone directory under
the name of the Sui Sung Match Company, Ltd. and this may
have had some connection with the belief of small traders
that the matches are of Japanese origin. This matter was
brought to the attention of the management of the Company
and they have taken steps to have the matter remedied in
the next issue of the telephone directory.
W. Duncan.
D. S. I.
Officer i/c Special Branch.

由特别调查员邓肯（R.S.I. Duncan）呈报，经罗伯逊督察长（Supt Tho Robertson）转呈

自本人1932年9月13日的报告以来，关于抵制美商远东火柴公司制造的火柴一事，并无新的重要情况发展。虽然上海仍能感受到抵制的影响，但并无加剧的迹象，火柴公司管理层相信，随着时间的推移，抵制将完全平息。那批在泉州被扣留的火柴货物，尽管美国公使已向福建省当局提出交涉，但仍被扣押。

位于布伦南路（Brenan Road）的美商远东火柴厂，在电话簿中仍以“瑞松火柴有限公司”（Sui Sung Match Company, Ltd.）的名义列出，这可能与小商贩认为该火柴系日货的看法有关。此事已提请公司管理层注意，他们已采取措施，在下一期电话簿中更正此事。
W. 邓肯。

Divisional Memo No. 46

Divisional Officers & Chief Inspectors etc.,
i/c Districts.

Political Meetings and/or Meetings to discuss
Boycott held on Licensed Premises.

Information has been received that the licensed premises
of the Great Eastern Hotel were on August 25, 1932, used for
a meeting which discussed matters concerned with the anti-
Japanese boycott which affected the business of an American
firm.

By allowing this meeting, the management of the hotel
contravened Clause No. 5 of the hotel license. It is very
desirable that there will be no repetition of this occurrence.

Divisional Officers should therefore instruct Chief
Inspectors etc., i/c of districts to warn their staffs to
take special precautions to ensure that no meetings to promote
boycotts or other political objects are allowed in hotels or
other licensed premises in their districts.

L. O. Springfield
Deputy Commissioner (Divisions).

GENERAL REGISTRY
No. C 262
19 / 3 / 32

September 19, 1932.

Sir,

I have the honour to acknowledge receipt of
your letter of September 1, on the subject of boycott
activities against the American Far Eastern Match Company,
Federal Incorporated, U.S.A.

In reply, I have the honour to inform you that
Police inquiries reveal that a meeting actually took place
at the Great Eastern Hotel on August 25, at which the
subject of the boycott of matches was discussed. No in-
formation is, however, available that the meeting was
continued on August 30.

I also have the honour to inform you that the
Police have for several months been endeavouring to prevent
the boycott of matches of the American Far Eastern Match
Company, and will continue to do so. Special measures
will, moreover, be taken to ensure that no further meetings
to promote this object are held in the Great Eastern Hotel
or other licensed premises.

In conclusion, I have the honour to state that
the Commissioner of Police is arranging that the file
giving an account of Police investigations into this matter
will be shown to you confidentially.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,
J. R. JONES
Secretary.

B. S. Cunningham, Esq.,
American Consul-General.

REPORT
Date Sept. 13, 1932.

Subject (in full) Boycott against American Matches.

Made by D.S.I. Duncan Forwarded by Jhu Robertson Supt

With reference to the letter from Mr. Cunningham,
U.S.A. Consul-General, to the Chairman of the Council
regarding meetings being held in the International
Settlement for the purpose of further boycott activities
against the American Far Eastern Match Company, enquiries
show that such a meeting did take place on August 25 as
stated, but no proof can be had that the meeting scheduled
for August 30 for the same purpose took place and none
have been known to have taken place since.

The whole question of the origin and system
employed in this boycott movement is covered in a
comprehensive manner in a report submitted by D.S. Tilton
dated June 13, 1932 (Attached).

From the correspondence and minutes of meetings
held in efforts to clear up this matter it appears as if
the boycott first originated in Chuanchow where Messrs
Boyd & Co (British) are agents for the matches in
question and that a Fokienese firm named Nan Chow & Company
with offices at 25 Rue du Consulat were behind the movement.
This is born out in a statement made to a foreign
representative of the Swedish-Chinese Export & Import
Company in the presence of Mr. Eugene Y.B. Kiang, a well
known Chinese lawyer acting for the American Far Eastern
Match Company, on August 17 and a meeting held in the
residence of a Mr. Li on Avenue Road. Mr. Liu, a committee
member of the National Salvation Federation, who was present
at the meeting, stated that they had definite proof that
the matches detained at Chuanchow were Japanese and they
(The Federation) claimed the $100,000 reward promised

由副督察邓肯（Duncan）撰写，经朱罗伯逊（Jhu Robertson）警司转呈

关于美国驻沪总领事坎宁安（Cunningham）先生致工部局董事会主席的信函，信中提及在国际租界内举行会议以进一步开展针对美商远东火柴公司（American Far Eastern Match Company）的抵制活动一事，经查证，正如信中所称，8月25日确实举行过此类会议，但无法获得证据证明原定于8月30日为同一目的举行的会议确实召开，且此后也未闻有此类会议举行。

关于此次抵制运动的起源及所采用的体系，D.S. 蒂尔顿（Tilton）于1932年6月13日提交的报告（附后）中已作了全面的阐述。

从为澄清此事而进行的通信往来及会议纪要来看，抵制运动似乎最初起源于泉州（Chuanchow），当地博伊德公司（Boyd & Co，英商）是涉案火柴的代理商，而一家名为南周公司（Nan Chow & Company，音译）的福建籍商行，其办事处位于领事馆路25号，是幕后推手。这一点在8月17日于爱文义路（Avenue Road）李某寓所举行的一次会议上得到证实，当时瑞典-中国进出口公司的一位外籍代表在场，代表美商远东火柴公司的知名华人律师江一平（Eugene Y.B. Kiang）先生也在场。出席该会议的全国救国会委员会成员刘某声称，他们有确凿证据证明在泉州被扣押的火柴是日本货，他们（救国会）要求兑现美商远东公司承诺的10万美元赏金，该赏金旨在奖励任何能证明其火柴源自日本的人。

Subject (in full) Report on activities of Shanghai Salvation Federation.

Made by D. S. Pryde. Forwarded by C. I. Tilling

Sir,
At 11 a.m. 7-9-32 a telephone message was received from Mr.
J. Wulsbery of American Far Eastern Match Company requesting the
services of a detective. D. S. Pryde attended and was informed that
that the "Shanghai Salvation Federation" had, since the early
part of July 1932, instigated a boycott of the matches manufac-
tured by this firm, on the pretext that these matches are of
Japanese manufacture.
This company bought the Sue Sung Match Company, which was a
Japanese concern, in 1928, and went into liquidation on December
1st 1931. On the morning of 7-9-32 an advertisement appeared in
a Japanese owned newspaper to the effect that this company was
still operating, and Mr. Wulfsberg considered that this advertise-
ment was inserted with a view to further the boycott. Copy of
the newspaper concerned attached.
Mr. Wulfsberg supplied the undersigned with a copy of their
their file on this matter and same is attached and forwarded for
instructions.

D. S. Pryde.

SHANGHAI.

Attention Mr. G. B. Pryde.

Dear Sirs,

Boycott Activities Against the Swedish-Chinese Exp. & Imp. Co.
and the American-Far Eastern Match Co.

We thank you for your courtesy in sending, at our request Mr. G. B. Pryde, to interview us this morning. As was explained to Mr. G. B. Pryde we find ourselves the victims of organized boycott against us and our goods.

One of the first days of July, this year, a quantity of 1,500 cartons of "Wheel" matches were detained by the Anti-Japanese Boycott Society at Chuanchiu. We have definite proof that this was done at the instigation of the Shanghai Salvation Federation. The matches have still not been released in spite of protests from the American and Swedish Consulates and Legations as well as from the Swedish and the American companies, through the Shanghai Chinese Chamber of Commerce and the Swedish and American Chambers of Commerce in Shanghai. The British and American consulates in Amoy have also filed protests, all without avail.

So as to avoid making this report too lengthy we enclose copies of various letters which are of interest in the case.

1. Letter addressed to Mr. Eugene Y. B. Kiang, Chinese barrister at law engaged by us to assist us in overcoming the boycott activities. This letter explains in detail the internal position between the Swedish and American companies.

2. Photographic copy of a letter written by the Swedish Match Co., Kobe, in October, 1928, relating to the purchase of the Sui Sung Match Co. by the Swedish Match Co. at that time - more than four years ago.

3. Letter received from the Shanghai Chinese Chamber of Commerce showing that the Chamber has received definite proof of the non-existence of Japanese interests in our matches.

敬启者：

关于针对瑞典-中国进出口公司及美商远东火柴公司的抵制活动

感谢贵方惠允，应我方请求派遣 G. B. Pryde 先生于今晨来访。正如向 G. B. Pryde 先生所解释的那样，我们发现自身成为针对我方及我方货物的有组织抵制的受害者。

今年7月初，1,500箱“轮牌”（Wheel）火柴在泉州（Chuanchiu）被抗日救国会扣押。我们有确凿证据证明，此举是在上海救国会的煽动下进行的。尽管美国及瑞典领事馆和公使馆，以及瑞典和美国公司通过上海华人总商会、上海瑞典商会和美国商会提出了抗议，厦门的英美领事馆也提出了抗议，但火柴至今仍未获释放，所有努力均无成效。

为避免本报告过于冗长，我们附上案件中相关的各类信件副本。

1. 致尤金·Y·B·江（Eugene Y. B. Kiang）先生的信函，江先生是我们聘请协助克服抵制活动的中国出庭律师。此信详细说明了瑞典公司与美国公司之间的内部关系。

2. 1928年10月瑞典火柴公司神户分公司所写信函的照片副本，内容涉及当时——即四年多前——瑞典火柴公司收购燧生火柴公司事宜。

3. 收到上海华人总商会的来信，显示该商会已收到确凿证据，证明我方火柴中不存在日本利益。

page_data.en:
The Swedish-Chinese Export & Import Co., Ltd. - 2 -

4. Letter from the Shanghai Chamber of Commerce to the
Anti-Japanese Boycott Society at Tsingkiang, directly
responsible for the detentions of our matches in
Fukien.

5. Minutes of a meeting with various boycott officials
in Shanghai.

6. Copy of a letter addressed by us to General Wu, Mayor
of Greater Shanghai.

7 and 8. Copies of letters addressed by us to the Danish
Legation, Peiping, acting as Swedish Legation in the
absence of the Swedish Charge d'Affaires.

9. Copy of a report from Clark's Inquiry Agency regarding
a meeting of the Boycott Society in Shanghai.

10. Copy of a letter addressed by us to the Chairman of
the General Chamber of Commerce, Shanghai, with
enclosure.

11. Copy of a letter addressed by us to the Shanghai-General
Chamber of Commerce.

12. Copies of a letter with enclosures received by us today
from the American Consulate at Amoy.

These various documents will definitely show that the
above named firms and their matches are being made the object
of an organized boycott, the real motives for which probably
lie in competition and definitely in the hopes of the boycotters
to get some money out of the company through blackmail. It is
quite evident that the anti-Japanese movement is here only used
as a cover for purposes of blackmailing us.

As will be noted matches have been detained in Chuanchiu
now for more than one month in spite of protests made to all and
any authorities possible. The boycott activities in Shanghai
have carried on for almost one year and if they are allowed to
continue they constitute a severe threat to our existence.

We therefore have the honour to solicit your assistance
and request that you do everything in your power to come to the
source of the trouble which undoubtedly lies in the activities
of the Shanghai Boycott Society.

The Sui Sung Match Co. which was Swedish owned since
1928 went into liquidation on the 1st of December, last year.
Today we find an advertisement in a Japanese paper of the Sui
Sung Match Co. advertising the Sui Sung matches to the Japanese
public. The advertisement has been definitely denied by the
staff of the Sui Sung Match Co. in liquidation. We have grounds
page_data.zh:
瑞典-中国进出口有限公司 - 2 -

4. 上海总商会致清江（Tsingkiang，音译）抗日救国会的信函，该会直接负责对我们在福建被扣火柴的处理。

5. 与上海各位抵制运动官员会议的纪要。

6. 我方致大上海市长吴将军的信函副本。

7 和 8. 我方致北平丹麦公使馆的信函副本，在瑞典代办缺席期间，该馆代行瑞典公使馆职能。

9. 克拉克调查社（Clark's Inquiry Agency）关于上海救国会会议的报告副本。

10. 我方致上海总商会主席的信函副本，附有附件。

11. 我方致上海总商会的信函副本。

12. 我方今日收到的厦门美国领事馆来函及附件副本。

这些文件将明确显示，上述公司及其火柴正成为有组织抵制的对象，其真实动机可能在于竞争，且抵制者明确希望通过敲诈从公司获取钱财。显而易见，反日运动在此仅被用作敲诈我们的幌子。

值得注意的是，尽管向所有可能的当局提出抗议，火柴在泉州已被扣押一个多月。上海的抵制活动已持续近一年，若任其继续，将对我们的生存构成严重威胁。

因此，我们荣幸地恳请贵方协助，并请求贵方竭尽全力追查祸源，这无疑在于上海救国会的活动。

燧生火柴公司自1928年起由瑞典人拥有，于去年12月1日进入清算程序。今日，我们在一份日文报纸上看到燧生火柴公司的广告，向日本公众推销燧生火柴。该广告已遭到处于清算状态的燧生火柴公司职员的明确否认。我们有理由

page_data.en:
The Swedish-Chinese Export & Import Co., Ltd. - 3 -

to believe that the advertisement has been inserted by the boy-
cotters in order to disprove our statements that the Sui Sung
Match Co. does no longer function since it went into liquidation
in 1931 in December. For various reasons the liquidation has not
yet been concluded. The newspaper in question was handed to Mr.
Pryde on his visit here today.

We should be much obliged if you would endeavour to
find out for our account who is responsible for the advertise-
ment.

Another matter of local interest which was mentioned to
Mr. Pryde is the fact that several local shops for instance the
Hai Chi (    ), corner of Chefoo Road and Thibet Road, is sell-
ing the "Lucky-Boy" matches of the American-Far Eastern Match Co.
at a price of two coppers per box, which is considerably below
our sales price. It is evident that there is an organization
endeavouring to ruin the business in this brand, particularly so,
as our men sent out to buy the whole stock of the mentioned shop
were refused to buy even a single package. Through this action
they are making our sales to other dealers exceedingly difficult,
since such dealers will claim that they cannot pay a higher price
than the matches are sold for in the local market. There is, of
course, no criminal act underlying the selling of our matches at
low prices, but we have no doubt that the same interests are
behind these activities as those trying to damage our business
through the boycott movement.

If there are any details that are not entirely clear
through this letter and its enclosures we shall be only too
pleased to receive your representatives to whom further ex-
planations might be made.

Yours faithfully,
行 洋 中 瑞
THE SWEDISH-CHINESE
EXPORT & IMPORT CO., LTD.
John Willsberg

瑞典中国进出口有限公司 - 3 -

相信该广告系抵制者所刊登，旨在驳斥我方关于“燧生火柴公司”（Sui Sung Match Co.）自1931年12月进入清算程序以来已不再运营的声明。由于种种原因，清算工作尚未结束。有关报纸已于今日普赖德先生（Mr. Pryde）来访时交予他。

如蒙贵方代为查明该广告的责任人，我们将不胜感激。

向普赖德先生提及的另一件本地关注事项是，几家本地商店，例如芝罘路（Chefoo Road）与西藏路（Thibet Road）拐角处的海记（Hai Chi，音译），正以每盒两枚铜板的价格出售美远东火柴公司（American-Far Eastern Match Co.）的“幸运男孩”（Lucky-Boy）牌火柴，该价格远低于我们的售价。显然，有一个组织正试图破坏该品牌的经营，尤其是当我们派人去购买上述商店的全部库存时，对方甚至拒绝出售单包火柴。通过此举，他们使得我们向其他经销商的销售变得极其困难，因为这些经销商会声称，他们无法支付高于本地市场火柴售价的价格。当然，低价销售我方火柴并不构成犯罪行为，但我们毫无疑问，这些活动背后的利益集团与试图通过抵制运动损害我方业务的集团相同。

若本函及其附件中有任何细节尚不清楚，我们非常乐意接待贵方代表，以便作进一步解释。

此致，
瑞典中国
进出口有限公司

Eugene Y. B. Kiang, Esq.,
Third Floor, 48 Szechuen Road,
Shanghai.

Dear Sir:

Report of our Shanghai-made Matches.

This company, the Swedish-Chinese Export & Import Co.
Ltd., commenced business in China and in Shanghai in 1919. The
company is a Swedish limited liability company, registered with
the local Swedish Consulate-General. Its share capital is
totally Swedish. Out of 1,000 shares, 996 are held by the
Swedish Match Co., Stockholm. Four shares are held by individ-
ual directors in the company, all Swedish.

We enclose the Directors' report of the Swedish Match
Company for the year 1930. Pages 9 and 10 of this report con-
tain the balance sheet as at December 31st, 1930. On page 10
will be seen the item of 996 shares in the Swedish-Chinese Exp.
& Imp. Co. Ltd. as an asset of the Swedish Match Company.

We also enclose a photographic copy of a certificate
issued by the Swedish Consulate-General at Shanghai on the 27th
October, 1931, certifying the Swedish origin of the matches
handled by the Swedish-Chinese Exp. & Imp. Co. Ltd., "Phoenix",
"Globe" and "Bridge" brands. All matches handled by the
Swedish-Chinese Exp. & Imp. Co. Ltd. are of Swedish origin,
made in Sweden and exported from the port of Gothenburg direct
to Shanghai, mostly by Swedish vessels. No matches under these
trade-marks have ever been imported from Japan, nor to our know-
ledge made in any country outside of Sweden. The Swedish-Chinese
have no Japanese employees and have no Japanese interests what-
ever.

We attach label specimens of the three labels for
quality matches made in Sweden and sold in China by the Swedish-
Chinese Exp. & Imp. Co. Ltd. At the side of the label speci-
mens are marked details as regards registration, etc., in China.
page_data.zh:
1932年8月16日。

江 Eugene Y. B. 先生，
上海四川路48号三楼。

尊敬的先生：

关于我方上海制造火柴的报告。

本公司，即瑞典中国进出口有限公司，于1919年开始在中国及上海开展业务。本公司是一家瑞典有限责任公司，已在当地瑞典总领事馆注册。其股本完全为瑞典所有。在1,000股股份中，996股由斯德哥尔摩的瑞典火柴公司（Swedish Match Co.）持有。其余4股由公司个别董事持有，均为瑞典人。

随函附上瑞典火柴公司1930年度董事报告。该报告第9页和第10页载有截至1930年12月31日的资产负债表。在第10页可以看到，瑞典中国进出口有限公司的996股股份被列为瑞典火柴公司的资产。

我们还附上1931年10月27日由驻上海瑞典总领事馆出具的一份证明书的影印件，证明瑞典中国进出口有限公司经营的“凤凰”（Phoenix）、“地球”（Globe）和“桥”（Bridge）牌火柴源自瑞典。瑞典中国进出口有限公司经营的所有火柴均原产于瑞典，在瑞典制造，并主要从哥德堡港由瑞典船只直接出口至上海。这些商标项下的火柴从未从日本进口过，据我们所知，也未在瑞典以外的任何国家制造。瑞典中国公司没有日本雇员，也没有任何日本利益关系。

随函附上瑞典中国进出口有限公司在中国销售的、在瑞典制造的优质火柴的三种标签样本。在标签样本旁标注了关于在中国注册等事宜的详细信息。

page_data.en:
The Cathay Match Co., Ltd.

The Swedish Match Company, having acquired match
monopolies in various European countries, had from the years
1927 and 1928 certain stocks of European-made matches which
they wished to dispose of in the markets of the Far East.
The Swedish Match Company objected to these matches being
handled by the Swedish-Chinese Exp. & Imp. Co. Ltd., as that
company was known to be dealing in Swedish-made matches only.
On these grounds, the Cathay Match Co. Ltd., was founded, the
Swedish-Chinese Exp. & Imp. Co. Ltd. representing that company
in China, as will be seen on the heading of our letter paper.

To begin with, the Cathay Match Co. imported various
brands of matches from several European countries, such as
Poland, Germany, Belgium, Jugo-Slavia and Czechoslovakia, etc.
No matches were ever imported by the Cathay Match Co. from
Japan. Some matches have, however, in earlier years been
imported from Japan by our Hongkong office. Such imports have
longsince been entirely stopped.

On the 1st January, 1931, duty on matches imported
into China was raised, for one class from 7-1/2% to 40% and
in a second class from Haikwan Tl.30 per unit of 50-gross
boxes to Gold Units 15.00. These increased customs duties,
as well as various other circumstances, caused us losses on
matches imported from Europe under the various Cathay Match
Company's brands, - i.e., not quality brands. Quite naturally,
our attention was then directed to the possibilities of manu-
facturing such matches in China, and when the manufacturing of
these brands was commenced early in 1931 at the local Sui Sing
factory in Shanghai, importation from Europe practically
ceased. It must be understood that at this time there existed
no hostile feeling between the Chinese and the Japanese.
There was no anti-Japanese boycott and the Chinese and Japanese
were dealing with one another uninterruptedly in various lines
of business.

We enclose herewith a photographic copy of a certif-
icate issued by the Swedish Consulate-General in Shanghai, dated
the 16th November, 1932, certifying the above statements.

We attach specimens of the various labels of the
Cathay Match Company's trade-marks. It will be seen that all
trade-marks are marked "Made in China", "Made in Poland", "Made
in Belgium", etc., in each case showing the origin of the manu-
facture. Beside the labels you will find information as to
registration in China, etc.
page_data.zh:
国泰火柴有限公司（The Cathay Match Co., Ltd.）

瑞典火柴公司在收购了欧洲多个国家的火柴垄断权后，从1927年和1928年起持有一定数量的欧洲制造火柴库存，希望将其处置到远东市场。瑞典火柴公司反对由瑞典中国进出口有限公司经营这些火柴，因为众所周知，该公司仅经营瑞典制造的火柴。基于此理由，成立了国泰火柴有限公司，瑞典中国进出口有限公司代表该公司在中国开展业务，正如我方信头所示。

起初，国泰火柴公司从波兰、德国、比利时、南斯拉夫和捷克斯洛伐克等几个欧洲国家进口各种品牌的火柴。国泰火柴公司从未从日本进口过火柴。然而，早些年我们的香港办事处曾从日本进口过少量火柴。此类进口早已完全停止。

1931年1月1日，进口到中国的光洋税提高，其中一类从7.5%提高到40%，另一类从每50大箱海关两30两提高到金单位15.00元。这些增加的关税以及其他各种情况，导致我们在以国泰火柴公司各品牌（即非优质品牌）进口的欧洲火柴上遭受损失。很自然，我们的注意力随后转向在中国制造此类火柴的可能性，当1931年初在上海本地的燧生（Sui Sing）工厂开始生产这些品牌时，从欧洲的进口实际上停止了。必须指出的是，当时中日之间并不存在敌对情绪。没有反日抵制运动，中国人在各种商业领域与日本人保持着不间断的往来。

随函附上1932年11月16日由驻上海瑞典总领事馆出具的一份证明书的影印件，以证实上述陈述。

随函附上国泰火柴公司各种商标的标签样本。可以看出，所有商标均标有“中国制造”、“波兰制造”、“比利时制造”等字样，在每种情况下都表明了制造产地。在标签旁边，您可以找到关于在中国注册等信息。

page_data.en:
-3-

The Sui Sung Match Co., Ltd.

In 1928, in connection with certain transactions made
in Japan between the Swedish Match Company and Japanese match
interests, all the shares of the Sui Sung Match Co., Ltd. were
bought by the Swedish Match Company. The Sui Sung Match Co.
was then running a match factory in Shanghai. This factory
was very badly fitted with machinery of old and inefficient
types. For various reasons, it was then decided to let the
Sui Sung Match Co. until further officially remain a Japanese
company. The registration in the Japanese Consulate-General
in Shanghai was maintained. All the shares were sold to the
Swedish Match Co., but the transfer was not completed. For
each share, however, we hold a trust deed in favor of the Swedish
Match Co. and a power of attorney in blank, both signed by the
various nominal shareholders. Shares, as well as trust deeds
and powers of attorney, are kept by us here in Shanghai. Since
1928, therefore, there was not a single cent of Japanese capital
invested in the Sui Sung Match Co. Ltd. At the time, there was
no reason for us to change the previous nationality of the company,
as the Chinese and Japanese were doing business freely with one
another.

The Sui Sung Match Co., Ltd. had stocks of matches manu-
factured by them under various trade-marks known on the market.
There were some Japanese employees in charge at the factory, and
at the time we had no suitable men with whom to replace them.
Some of these employees had long term contracts, and it would
have entailed considerable expenditure to dispense with their
services at the time. This explains why the Sui Sung Match Co.
Ltd. was then until further maintained as a Japanese company,
although, as has been pointed out above, there was absolutely
no Japanese capital invested in the company. The shares are now
in our office and may be inspected by you or by any parties con-
cerned who are interested in verifying the statements made above.

During the years 1928-1932, the Shanghai Sui Sung
factory was equipped with new and modern match making machin-
ery. The factory was in every detail rebuilt and outfitted
with the best machinery most, imported by us direct from Sweden.
For this machinery, the Sui Sung Match Co. Ltd., whose books
were kept separately, was debited, but no payments were made.
The company, therefore, accumulated a considerable debt to us.
This was of little concern, as in effect the company was owned
by Swedish interests.

Then, in the beginning of 1932, the Japanese military
authorities made a sudden importation of these Japanese matches
impossible, and attention was directed to the possibility of
making matches under the same trademarks in China. As we
page_data.zh:
-3-

燧生火柴有限公司（The Sui Sung Match Co., Ltd.）

1928年，随着瑞典火柴公司与日本火柴利益集团在日本进行的某些交易，燧生火柴有限公司的全部股份被瑞典火柴公司收购。当时，燧生火柴公司在上海经营一家火柴厂。该工厂的设备非常糟糕，使用的是陈旧且效率低下的机器。由于各种原因，当时决定让燧生火柴公司在正式层面上继续保留为日本公司。其在上海日本总领事馆的注册得以维持。所有股份均出售给瑞典火柴公司，但转让手续并未完成。然而，对于每一股股份，我们都持有以瑞典火柴公司为受益人的信托契据以及空白授权委托书，均由各位名义股东签署。股份以及信托契据和授权委托书均由我们保存在上海。因此，自1928年以来，燧生火柴有限公司中没有一分钱是日本资本投入的。当时，我们没有理由改变公司此前的国籍身份，因为中日双方正在自由地进行商业往来。

燧生火柴有限公司拥有以其在市场上知名的各种商标生产的火柴库存。工厂里有一些日本雇员负责管理，当时我们没有合适的人选来替换他们。其中一些雇员签有长期合同，当时解雇他们将需要相当大的开支。这就解释了为什么燧生火柴有限公司当时在正式层面上继续维持为日本公司，尽管如上所述，该公司中绝对没有任何日本资本投入。股份现在位于我们的办公室，供您或任何有兴趣核实上述陈述的相关方查阅。

在1928年至1932年期间，上海燧生工厂配备了新的现代化火柴制造机械。工厂在每一个细节上都进行了重建，并配备了最好的机械，大部分由我们直接从瑞典进口。对于这些机械，账目独立核算的燧生火柴有限公司被记入借方，但未进行付款。因此，该公司对我们积累了巨额债务。这无关紧要，因为实际上该公司由瑞典利益集团所有。

后来，在1932年初，日本军事当局突然使这些日本火柴的进口成为不可能，注意力便转向在中国使用相同商标制造火柴的可能性。正如我们

page_data.en:
-4-

had already fitted the local Shanghai factory with modern machinery, making it the best factory in the Far East, it is only natural that manufacturing orders were placed with the factory for matches under our well-known trade-marks earlier manufactured only in Europe. The inscriptions on the labels, "Made in Poland", "Made in Belgium", etc., were of course altered to "Made in China."

Later in 1931, after this manufacture had been well commenced, and the goods were also well-known on the market, the Sino-Japanese conflict developed, and the boycott of Japanese goods was commenced. Quite naturally, under the circumstances, we found our matches made in the local factory boycotted. We explained to the authorities the true position, and requested the assistance of the Nanking Government. At our request, the Swedish Chargé d'Affaires proceeded to Nanking and filed our application for assistance from the Nanking Government in the troubles which developed. We quote from a letter dated the 11th November, 1931, and addressed to His Excellency, Mr. Chinglun Frank W. Lee, Minister of Foreign Affairs, at Nanking, as follows:

"The matches made in China for the account of 'the Cathay Match Company' are manufactured by the 'Sui Sung Company', a company registered in the Japanese Consulate-General in Shanghai, but, since 1929, in effect controlled by the 'Swedish-Chinese Export & Import Company'. The Chinese authorities are well aware of this, and if the Swedish company has hesitated to advertise this fact, the reason has been the wish to avoid complications in the dealings between the Japanese Consulate-General and the factory management, which is still partly Japanese."

As will be seen there was no secret made of the fact that the Sui Sung Match Co. Ltd. was in effect controlled by us.

In the matches manufactured, there was consequently no Japanese interest of any kind. Nevertheless, we found the matches rapidly being boycotted and being detained by boycott associations in various places in China. We then got in touch with the Shanghai boycott association, who sent an investigating committee, which our representative met at the office of the China Merchants' Steam Navigation Company's Lower Wharf, where our matches were then stored. All the facts regarding the manufacture of our matches in China were then given to the investigating committee, and they advised us that in order to avoid any further complications we had better complete the transfer of the Sui Sung Match Co. Ltd.. As long as the Sui Sung Match Co. Ltd. was known in China as a Japanese concern,
page_data.zh:
-4-

已经用现代机械装备了上海本地工厂，使其成为远东最好的工厂，将此前仅在欧洲制造的知名商标项下的火柴生产订单下达给该工厂是自然而然的。标签上的“波兰制造”、“比利时制造”等字样当然也改为“中国制造”。

1931年晚些时候，在此类生产已良好启动且商品在市场上也已广为人知之后，中日冲突爆发，抵制日货运动开始。在这种情况下，很自然，我们发现本地工厂制造的火柴遭到抵制。我们向当局解释了真实情况，并请求南京政府提供协助。应我方请求，瑞典代办前往南京，并就发展中出现的麻烦提交了我方寻求南京政府协助的申请。我们引用1931年11月11日致南京外交部长李景伦·弗兰克·W·李（Chinglun Frank W. Lee）阁下的一封信中的内容如下：

“为‘国泰火柴公司’账户在中国制造的火柴由‘燧生公司’生产，这是一家在上海日本总领事馆注册的公司，但自1929年以来，实际上由‘瑞典中国进出口公司’控制。中国当局对此十分清楚，如果瑞典公司一直犹豫未公开宣传这一事实，原因是希望避免与仍部分由日本人组成的工厂管理层在与日本总领事馆打交道时产生复杂情况。”

由此可见，燧生火柴有限公司实际上由我方控制这一事实并非秘密。

因此，在所制造的火柴中，没有任何形式的日本利益。尽管如此，我们发现火柴迅速遭到抵制，并被中国各地的抵制协会扣留。随后我们与上海抵制协会取得联系，该协会派遣了一个调查委员会，我方代表在中国招商局轮船公司下码头（Lower Wharf）的办公室与该委员会会面，当时我们的火柴就储存在那里。随后向调查委员会提供了关于我们在中国制造火柴的所有事实，他们建议我们，为了避免任何进一步的复杂情况，最好完成燧生火柴有限公司的转让手续。只要燧生火柴有限公司在中国被视为日本商号，

page_data.en:
-5-

we would continually find our matches boycotted. Negotiations
were at once entered upon with the Swedish Match Company's offices
in Stockholm. It was decided by the head office that the local
factory in Shanghai should be sold to American interests. On
the 31st December, 1931, the American-Far Eastern Match Co. Federal
Inc. U.S.A. was incorporated at Washington. Out of that company's
2,500 shares, 2,498 are held by the International Match Corporation
of New York in trust for the Swedish Match Company. The Inter-
national Match Corporation, although an American company, is in
reality a daughter company of the Swedish Match Company and until
the present time was controlled by that company.

In order to avoid any future complications, all traces
of anything Japanese were carefully erased. Any Japanese account-
ing books were destroyed. We went so far as to destroy or sell
Japanese scales and instruments. The few remaining Japanese fore-
men at the factory were discharged and replaced by Swedish foremen.
The manufacture of matches under the Cathay Match Company's labels
continued exactly as before. A long time previously, all manufact-
ure of the matches under the original Sui Sung Labels had been dis-
continued completely.

Between matches manufactured prior to the 1st January,
1932, and matches manufactured thereafter, there exists, therefore,
no difference whatever, except in the fact of the time of manufact-
ure. The factory is the same; the machinery employed is the same;
the workmen - about 600 Chinese - are the same. The capital in-
vested in the factory previously and afterwards was in both cases
absolutely not Japanese, and no Japanese concern or individuals
had previously or afterwards any financial or economic interest
whatever in the manufacture or in the Sui Sung Match Co. Docu-
mentary proof of all the above statements can be supplied by us.

The Ninth District Office of the Consolidated Tax Admin-
istration of the Ministry of Finance, situated in Robison Road,
Shanghai, was directly in charge of the control of the manufacture
at the factory for the purpose of taxation. Their representative
at the factory had a chop used by him personally in any actions
involving matters in which the Tax Office were interested. This
chop contained the information that he was the representative of
the Sui Sung Match Company. The chop therefore includes the
Chinese characters for "Sui Sung". Due to an oversight mainly,
a new chop was not given to this tax representative immediately
after the sale of the factory to the American interests. A new
chop was not supplied until at the end of February or the begin-
ning of March. We have inquired from the Ninth District office
of the Consolidated Tax Administration for the actual date, which
we expect to be able to give you in a day or two. All matches
delivered during the months of January and February, and also in
the beginning of March, were therefore sent out with the chop in-
cluding the Chinese characters for "Sui Sung", although the manu-
facture was actually that of the American-Far Eastern Match Co.
page_data.zh:
-5-

我们将不断发现我们的火柴遭到抵制。我们随即与斯德哥尔摩的瑞典火柴公司办事处进行了谈判。总公司决定将上海的地方工厂出售给美国利益方。1931年12月31日，美亚火柴有限公司（American-Far Eastern Match Co. Federal Inc. U.S.A.）在华盛顿注册成立。在该公司的2,500股股份中，有2,498股由纽约的国际火柴公司（International Match Corporation）代瑞典火柴公司持有。国际火柴公司虽然是一家美国公司，但实际上是瑞典火柴公司的子公司，并且直到目前一直由该公司控制。

为了避免将来出现任何纠纷，所有带有日本痕迹的事物都被仔细清除。任何日本的会计账簿均被销毁。我们甚至销毁或卖掉了日本制的秤和仪器。工厂里仅存的几名日本工头被解雇，并由瑞典工头取代。使用华昌火柴公司（Cathay Match Company）商标的火柴生产完全照旧进行。早在很久以前，使用原“燧生”（Sui Sung）商标的火柴生产就已完全停止。

因此，在1932年1月1日之前生产的火柴与此后生产的火柴之间，除了生产时间不同外，没有任何区别。工厂是同一个；使用的机器是同一批；工人——大约600名中国人——也是同一批人。此前和此后投入工厂的资本绝对都不是日本资本，此前和此后没有任何日本企业或个人在“燧生”火柴公司或其生产中拥有任何财务或经济利益。我们可以提供上述所有陈述的文件证明。

财政部统税局上海第九区办事处位于罗宾森路（Robison Road），直接负责出于征税目的对工厂生产进行监管。他们在工厂的代表拥有一枚个人印章，用于涉及税务局利益事项的任何行动。这枚印章包含他是燧生火柴公司代表的信息。因此，该印章包含中文“燧生”字样。主要由于疏忽，在工厂出售给美国利益方后，没有立即向这位税务代表发放新印章。直到2月底或3月初才提供了新印章。我们已向统税局第九区办事处查询确切日期，预计在一两天内能告知贵方。因此，1月和2月以及3月初交付的所有火柴，虽然实际上是由美亚火柴公司生产的，但发出的货物上都盖有包含中文“燧生”字样的印章。

page_data.en:
-6-

However, as in both cases there was no Japanese interest connected
with the manufacture, this should be of little importance.

The factory had registered with the Tax Administration
various so-called "outside factory godowns" in Shanghai, in which
godowns the factory was permitted to store matches until further
without payment of consolidated excise tax. A permit to transfer to
outside godowns is regularly being pasted on each package of matches
and chopped by the tax representative at the factory. On the matches
transferred from the factory in the beginning of the year there
appears, consequently, the chop containing the "Sui Sung" characters,
although in effect the manufacture was later than the 1st of January,
1938, when the American company commenced functioning.

The godowns held prior to the 1st of January are the same
as those held after the 1st of January. The brands of matches were
exactly the same, and deliveries to the godowns were made both before
and after the 1st of January. The cargo was, therefore, to some ex-
tent mixed in our godowns. We saw very little reason to keep the cargo
go separate, as the brands were the same and the machinery and the
methods of manufacture were identical. When these matches were later
sold, we were aware of the fact that the chop containing the "Sui
Sung" characters, which was on most cases put there after the first
of January, might cause us trouble. The tax office representative
was aware of the fact that the chop in itself was false, as it was,
in most cases, actually dated after the 1st January. With the know-
ledge of the tax representative, and often in his presence, tax stamps
were later, at the time of tax payment, pasted above the permit for
transport. Since this permit was to the effect of allowing the goods
to be stored in the outside godowns without tax payment, the permit
became automatically void and of no consequence at the moment of tax
payment. The pasting of the tax stamps above the previous transport
permit, consequently, was in no way an attempt to hide the origin
of these American-made matches. The chop of the tax representative
had not been altered - as it should have been . When tax was paid by
the American company the tax stamps were therefore pasted above the
"Sui Sung" characters which had been wrongly stamped on American
goods.

As has already been said, matches were transferred to the
same godowns before and after the American company took over the manu-
facture. As the matches in the godowns were not stored separately,
they have been mixed to some extent and treated alike as regards the
pasting of the tax stamps. Only in the case of manufacture later
than February, 1938, when the Tax Office representative's chop had
been altered, the cargo was placed in separate godowns, whereby it
could not be mixed up with the other lots.

It has been reported to us that the Anti-Japanese Boycott
Associations in Fukien have discovered some chop on the cargo show-
ing the "Sui Sung" characters. In that event some quantities of
our matches have been detained by these Associations.

The above statements and explanations will have demonstrated
definitely that - whether old or new cargo is concerned - there is in

然而，由于在这两种情况下，生产均不涉及日本利益，这应该无关紧要。

该工厂已在税务局注册了上海各个所谓的“厂外仓库”，工厂获准在这些仓库中储存火柴，暂时无需缴纳统税。转运至厂外仓库的许可证通常贴在每包火柴上，并由工厂的税务代表盖章。因此，在年初从工厂转运的火柴上，出现了包含“燧生”字样的印章，尽管实际上这些火柴的生产日期晚于1938年1月1日，即美国公司开始运营之时。

1月1日之前持有的仓库与1月1日之后持有的仓库相同。火柴的品牌完全相同，且在1月1日之前和之后都向仓库进行了交货。因此，我们的仓库中的货物在某种程度上混合在一起。鉴于品牌相同，机器和生产方法也一致，我们认为几乎没有理由将货物分开存放。当这些火柴后来售出时，我们意识到，大多数情况下在1月1日之后加盖的包含“燧生”字样的印章可能会给我们带来麻烦。税务局代表知道该印章本身是错误的，因为在大多数情况下，其实际日期是在1月1日之后。在税务代表知情且经常在其在场的情况下，后来在缴纳税款时，印花税票被贴在运输许可证上方。由于该许可证的作用是允许货物在未缴税的情况下储存在厂外仓库，因此在缴纳税款的那一刻，该许可证自动失效且不再具有任何效力。因此，将印花税票贴在之前的运输许可证上方，绝非试图隐藏这些美国制造火柴的来源。税务代表的印章并未像应该做的那样进行更改。因此，当美国公司缴纳税款时，印花税票被贴在了错误地盖在美国货物上的“燧生”字样之上。

如前所述，在美国公司接管生产之前和之后，火柴都被转运到相同的仓库。由于仓库中的火柴没有分开存放，它们在某种程度上混合在一起，并且在粘贴印花税票方面受到同等对待。只有在1938年2月之后生产的情况下，当税务局代表的印章已更改时，货物才被放入单独的仓库，从而不会与其他批次混淆。

据向我们报告，福建的反日抵制协会在货物上发现了一些显示“燧生”字样的印章。在这种情况下，我们的一些火柴已被这些协会扣留。

上述陈述和解释将明确表明——无论是旧货还是新货——在生产中绝

no way any Japanese interest connected with the manufacture.
The fact that a chop containing the "Sui Sung" characters is
found on part of the cargo is, therefore, of no significance,
whether the chop was put there before or after the 1st January
this year.

After the American-Far Eastern Match Co. took over
the factory, that company registered in Nanking one trade-mark
of their own, "Lucky Boy", of which a sample is attached. The
Cathay Match Co. has also in 1932 received registration of a
new trade-mark, the "Tiger" brand, of which a sample is also
enclosed. The manufacture of these two brands was commenced
only in May and June of this year.

The anti-Japanese boycott is directed against Japanese
goods. The fundamental fact remains absolutely indisputable
that matches sold by us and by the American-Far Eastern Match Co.,
whether under the Cathay Match Company's or the American-Far
Eastern Match Company's trade-marks, are definitely not Japanese,
and that in the manufacture of those matches, whether prior to or
after the 1st of January this year, there has been involved not
a single cent of Japanese invested capital. These fundamental
facts can be proven by us and sworn to in any court.

Under the circumstances, it is evident that the anti-
Japanese boycott, in affecting our goods, is being misdirected.
We quite realize the reasons for the activities of the Anti-
Japanese Boycott Committees against us, but it nevertheless re-
mains a fact that they are laboring under misunderstandings
which are causing severe damage to the Swedish and American com-
panies, both of whom are of friendly nationalities to the Chinese
people, and both of whom are in no way connected with Japanese
interests.

Further, as a very important point in this connection
we wish to point out the fact that as a consequence, of our
matches being boycotted no single Japanese subject or concern will
suffer any loss whatsoever. No destruction of our matches as
threatened will in any way inflict damage to Japanese interests.
The sufferers, besides the Swedish and American companies, will
be the labourers at the factory as well as the numerous shop
keepers dealing with our Chinese-American goods.

In fairness to our dealers it must be said that they
have regularly requested and received documentary proof of the
non-Japanese origin of our matches. They have thereby given
evidence of their personal interests which in every case is in
agreement with the interests of National Salvation.

We thank you for your suggestion that you ask the Cham-
ber of Commerce and the National Salvation Association to appoint
a committee, on which you will represent us, which committee will
carefully discuss the situation, and after being given all the

因此，部分货物上发现有包含“燧生”字样的印章这一事实，无论该印章是在今年1月1日之前还是之后盖上的，都无关紧要。

在美亚火柴公司接管工厂后，该公司在南京注册了其自己的一个商标“Lucky Boy”（幸运男孩），样品附后。华昌火柴公司也在1932年注册了一个新商标“Tiger”（虎牌）品牌，样品亦随函附上。这两个品牌的生产仅在今年5月和6月开始。

反日抵制是针对日本货物的。根本事实绝对无可争议：由我们和美亚火柴公司销售的火柴，无论是使用华昌火柴公司还是美亚火柴公司的商标，都绝对不是日本货，而且在这些火柴的生产中，无论是在今年1月1日之前还是之后，都没有涉及哪怕一分钱的日本投资资本。这些基本事实可以由我们证明，并可在任何法庭宣誓作证。

在这种情况下，显然反日抵制在影响我们的货物时被误导了。我们充分理解反日抵制委员会针对我们开展活动的原因，但事实仍然是，他们处于误解之中，这对瑞典和美国公司造成了严重损害，这两家公司都是中国人民的友好国家，且与日本利益毫无关联。

此外，作为与此相关的一个非常重要的点，我们希望指出这样一个事实：由于我们的火柴遭到抵制，没有任何日本臣民或企业会遭受任何损失。正如所威胁的那样，销毁我们的火柴绝不会损害日本利益。受害者除了瑞典和美国公司外，还将包括工厂的工人以及众多经销我们中美商品的店主。

公平起见，必须指出，我们的经销商定期要求并收到了关于我们火柴非日本起源的文件证明。他们由此证明了他们的个人利益，这在每种情况下都与救国利益相一致。

感谢您建议请商会和救国会任命一个委员会，由您代表我们参加，该委员会将仔细讨论局势，并在获悉所有

Translation
Copy of letter from the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, Shanghai to
the boycott society at Tsinkiang.

September 1, 1932. (4)

The Anti-Japanese Boycott Society.
Tsinkiang.

Dear Sirs,

In reply to our telegraphic request for an investigation
for your account of the Cathay Match Company's matches detained by
you, we sent you on the 26th August a telegram based on the statements
made by the American-Far Eastern Match Company.

Later, the Swedish-Consulate at Shanghai, the Swedish Chamber
of Commerce, the Swedish-Chinese Ex. & Imp. Co. and the American
Chamber of Commerce, Shanghai, have all written us separately on this
matter, giving an open review of the purchase of the factory, whereby
the truth of this case is revealed in every detail. The following are
the main points for your information.

All the shares of the Japanese Sui Sung Match Co. were
bought by the Cathay Match Co., belonging to the Swedish Match Co.,
in 1928. The registration of the company at the Japanese consulate
was, however, retained, as there was no Sino-Japanese trouble at that
time. There were also some Japanese employees in charge of the factory.
Due to increase of customs duties in the beginning of 1931 whereby
the imported matches had to pay heavier duties, the Cathay Match Co.
placed manufacturing orders with the Sui Sung factory, bought by them,
for matches under trade marks earlier manufactured in Europe. The
inscription on the labels "Made in Poland", "Made in Belgium", etc.,
were then altered to "Made in China". The factory had been refitted
with modern match-making machinery.

In the autumn, 1931, as a consequence of the Manchurian
affair, the matches made in the Sui Sung factory were found boycotted.
The Shanghai Boycott Society after an investigation of the purchase
of the factory, advised the company to complete the transfer of the
Sui Sung Match Co. in order to avoid any further complications. Nego-
tiations were then entered upon between the company and their head
office. On the 31st December, 1931, the Sui Sung factory was sold to
the American-Far Eastern Match Co., an American firm incorporated
at Washington. All the Japanese foremen were discharged and manufac-
ture of Sui Sung's brands stopped. The manufacture of the matches
under the Cathay Match Co's labels continued exactly as before. The
American company did not take over any matches under the original Sui
Sung's trade marks registered prior to their being taken over in 1928.

As will be seen from the above, the factory was Japanese
registered and Swedish owned since 1928 until the end of 1931. From
the 1st of January, 1932, even the registration which was until then
maintained has been changed.

1932年9月1日。(4)

致：
镇江
抗日抵制会

敬启者：

关于我方此前电请贵方调查由贵方扣留的中华火柴公司（Cathay Match Company）火柴一事，我方已于8月26日根据美亚远东火柴公司（American-Far Eastern Match Company）所作的陈述，向贵方去电说明。

此后，瑞典驻上海领事馆、瑞典商会、瑞中进出口公司（Swedish-Chinese Ex. & Imp. Co.）以及上海美国商会均就此事项分别致函我方，对工厂收购过程进行了公开审查，从而使本案真相得以详尽披露。现将主要要点列述如下，供贵方参考。

日本燧生火柴公司（Sui Sung Match Co.）的全部股份于1928年被隶属于瑞典火柴公司（Swedish Match Co.）的中华火柴公司收购。然而，由于当时中日之间并无纠纷，该公司在日本领事馆的注册得以保留。工厂内亦有一些日籍雇员负责管理。鉴于1931年初关税增加，导致进口火柴需缴纳更重的税款，中华火柴公司向其收购的燧生工厂下达了生产订单，生产此前在欧洲制造的商标项下的火柴。标签上原有的“波兰制造”、“比利时制造”等字样随后被改为“中国制造”。该工厂已重新装配了现代化的火柴制造机械。

1931年秋，作为满洲事变的结果，燧生工厂生产的火柴遭到抵制。上海抵制会在调查工厂收购情况后，建议该公司完成燧生火柴公司的转让手续，以避免任何进一步的复杂情况。随后，该公司与其总公司展开了谈判。1931年12月31日，燧生工厂被出售给美亚远东火柴公司，这是一家在华盛顿注册的美国公司。所有日籍工头均被解雇，燧生品牌的生产停止。中华火柴公司商标项下的火柴生产则完全照旧继续。美国公司并未接管任何在原燧生公司于1928年被收购之前注册的原有燧生商标项下的火柴。

由上可见，该工厂自1928年至1931年底期间，虽为日本注册，但归瑞典所有。自1932年1月1日起，甚至连此前一直维持的注册信息也已变更。

The chop used by the tax representative at the factory
after its being taken over by the American interests still contained
the "Sui Sung" characters, as a new chop was not supplied until the
end of February or beginning of March. Regarding this fact the
Consolidated Tax Bureau for Kiangsu, Chekiang and Anhwei has also
given explanations.

We are also informed by the Swedish-Chinese Exp. & Imp.
Co. that they represent the Cathay Match Co. and are sales agents
for the American-Far Eastern Match Co., Federal Inc. U.S.A., which
company is a manufacturing company only.

The case is thus made perfectly clear. We therefore give
you a detailed reply and request that the goods detained be released.

Yours truly,

REPORT OF CONFERENCES

with Mr. Eugene Y. Kiang, Mr. Wang, Chairman of the
Chinese Chamber of Commerce, Mr. Yang and Mr. Liu,
Committee Members of the Standing Committee of the
National Salvation Federation, Shanghai.

Held at Shanghai, 17th August 1932

According to arrangements, I was to meet Mr. Kiang,
the Chinese lawyer retained by us to assist us in overcoming the
boycott troubles in Fukien, at 12 o'clock in his office, on the
17th August. Shortly before 12 M. I received a telephone call
asking that I meet him in the Shanghai District Court on North
Chekiang Road. I met Mr. Kiang there at 12 o'clock and after
a short while we went to the Chinese Chamber of Commerce to see
Mr. Wang, the Chairman.

Mr. Wang did not appear until nearly 1 o'clock. In
the meantime, while we were waiting for him to arrive, Mr. Kiang
telephoned Mr. Li, one of the committee members of the National
Salvation Federation, and made an appointment with him at his
home on Avenue Road. Mr. Li had been sick for a few days, but
stated that he was now well and could receive Mr. Kiang. Mr.
Kiang then asked over the telephone whether he could bring a
foreigner with him. It was evident from the reply that Mr. Li
was not pleased with the idea, but the reply was nevertheless
affirmative.

When Mr. Wang, the Chairman of the Chamber of Commerce,
arrived, various documents were demonstrated to him to prove the
American origin and/or ownership of the matches shipped to Fukien
and detained there. He agreed that he realized that there was
no Japanese interest in the matches shipped by us, and stated that
he had already given all his secretaries instructions to that effect
so that they would know the origin of the matches in case the matter
was brought up in the Chamber.

We then left for Mr. Li's house on Avenue Road. After
waiting some few minutes, Mr. Li's son informed us that the doctor
had advised him not to see us. Instead they had telephoned for
Mr. Liu, another member of the committee, who would see us. Mr.
Liu arrived.

Definite proof of the Swedish ownership since 1928 of
the Sui Sung Match Co. and the American ownership of the Shanghai
factory of that company from the 1st January, 1932, was demon-
strated to Mr. Liu. Mr. Liu stated that he was already aware
of these facts and that they were not the point - the point of
interest was centered around a report from Chuanhow that cargo
had been found and detained carrying a shop showing the Sui Sung
characters and the date "September, 1931", while, he alleged, we
had informed them that the American-Far Eastern Match Co. had not
taken over any stocks of Japanese matches. I replied that our

时间：1932年8月17日
地点：上海

按照安排，我应于8月17日12点在其办公室会见我方聘请的中国律师江先生，以协助我们克服在福建的抵制麻烦。临近中午12点时，我接到一个电话，要求我在北浙江路上海特区地方法院与他见面。我于12点在那里见到了江先生，片刻之后，我们前往上海总商会去见王主席。

王主席直到将近1点钟才出现。在此期间，当我们等待他到达时，江先生致电全国救国联合会委员之一李先生，约定在其位于爱文义路（Avenue Road）的家中会面。李先生已病数日，但称现已痊愈，可以接待江先生。江先生随后通过电话询问是否可以带一名外国人同往。从答复中可以明显看出，李先生对此并不高兴，但答复仍然是肯定的。

当总商会王主席到达时，我们向他展示了各种文件，以证明运往福建并在那里被扣的火柴的美资来源和/或所有权。他承认他意识到我们装运的火柴中没有任何日资利益，并表示他已向所有秘书发出相应指示，以便在总商会提及此事时，他们能知晓火柴的来源。

随后我们前往爱文义路李先生家。等待了几分钟后，李先生的儿子告诉我们，医生建议他不要见客。相反，他们打电话叫来了委员会的另一位成员刘先生来见我们。刘先生到达了。

information was quite correct, - by "Japanese matches" of the
Sui Sung Match Co., we naturally did not mean matches under
the Swedish trade-marks belonging to the Cathay Match Co., but
meant matches under known Japanese trade-marks such as "Phonograph",
"Monkey", "Peach", etc. We could find no reason whatever for
calling matches under Swedish trade-marks, made by Chinese laborers
in a Swedish owned factory in China, "Japanese". Some stocks of
such matches were, of course, included in the running factory when
it was purchased by the American-Far Eastern Match Co., partly in
the form of half-finished goods and partly in the form of finished
goods in godowns belonging to the factory.

Mr. Liu then inquired the reasons why the American com-
pany had not merely taken over the business of the Sui Sung com-
pany. I replied that the American company could not possibly
take over the business of the Sui Sung company, as the American
company was not willing to take over any but easily accessible
assets in Shanghai. The Sui Sung Match Co. had already prev-
iously gone into liquidation, and sold to the American company
only their Shanghai assets directly connected with the factory
in Shanghai.

Mr. Liu then claimed that, as the Sui Sung Match Co.
had been managed by Japanese individuals, the real effect of the
action of the Swedish Match Co. had been that the Swedish Match
Co. had lent itself to financing a Japanese undertaking in Shanghai.
My reply was that this was decidedly incorrect, as we could give
them definite proof that not only the financing, but the actual
management, lay entirely in our hands. Mr. Liu next inquired
the reason why the Japanese management, in such case, had not been
done away with immediately after the Swedish Match Co. had bought
the factory in June, 1928. My reply to this question was that
the Sui Sung Match Co. at the time was a running concern, with
a certain market and a certain amount of good will attached and
that their Japanese trade-marks were known in the market. They
further had Japanese individuals employed under long term con-
tracts, which we could not possibly then cancel without taking
considerable losses. Also, if the factory were immediately to
be run as a Swedish factory, it would be impossible to take over
any of the good will attached to the Japanese labels. Besides,
it was at that time already decided that the Sui Sung company
should not remain a Japanese company, but correspondence with the
head office was continuously proceeding as to the plans for the
future of the factory. Due to various reasons, it was not de-
cided until toward the end of 1931 what should be done with the
factory. The decision was, of course, prompted by the difficult-
ies due to the anti-Japanese boycott.

Mr. Liu had no more questions to ask. I then made the
following statement:

"Since you gentlemen now must perfectly well realize,
in accordance with the definite proof laid before you, that since
June, 1928, there has not been one copper's value of Japanese
page_data.zh:
-2-

信息完全正确——就燧生火柴公司的“日货火柴”而言，我们自然不是指属于中华火柴公司的瑞典商标项下的火柴，而是指诸如“留声机”（Phonograph）、“猴牌”（Monkey）、“桃牌”（Peach）等知名的日本商标项下的火柴。我们找不到任何理由将由中国工人在瑞典所有的中国工厂内生产的、使用瑞典商标的火柴称为“日货”。当然，在美亚远东火柴公司收购该正在运营的工厂时，此类火柴的部分库存也被包括在内，部分以半成品形式存在，部分以成品形式存放在属于该工厂的仓库中。

刘先生随后询问，美国公司为何没有仅仅接管燧生公司的业务。我回答说，美国公司不可能接管燧生公司的业务，因为美国公司不愿意接管除上海易于处置的资产以外的任何资产。燧生火柴公司此前已进入清算程序，仅将其与上海工厂直接相关的上海资产出售给了美国公司。

刘先生随后声称，由于燧生火柴公司由日籍人士管理，瑞典火柴公司行动的实际效果是，瑞典火柴公司沦为为上海的一家日资企业提供融资的工具。我的回答是，这种说法绝对不正确，因为我们可以向他们提供确凿证据，证明不仅融资，而且实际管理权完全掌握在我们手中。刘先生接着询问，既然如此，为何在瑞典火柴公司于1928年6月收购工厂后，没有立即撤换日籍管理层。我对这个问题的回答是，当时的燧生火柴公司是一家正在运营的企业，拥有一定的市场和一定的商誉，且其日本商标在市场上为人所知。此外，他们还雇佣了签有长期合同的日籍人员，如果我们当时取消合同，必将遭受重大损失。而且，如果工厂立即作为瑞典工厂运营，就不可能接管依附于日本标签的任何商誉。此外，当时已决定燧生公司不应继续作为一家日本公司，但关于工厂未来的计划，与总公司的通信一直在持续进行。由于各种原因，直到1931年底才决定如何处理该工厂。做出这一决定的原因，当然是出于因抗日抵制而产生的困难。

刘先生不再有提问。随后我作了如下陈述：

“既然各位先生现在根据呈交给你们的确凿证据，必须充分认识到，自1928年6月以来，没有一文钱的日资

page_data.en:
capital invested in the Sui Sung Match Co., and as the matches
now in question are under Swedish trade-marks, as the manufacture
is financed by Swedish or American capital, as the labor is thor-
oughly Chinese and the raw materials almost exclusively non-
Japanese, there would exist no acceptable grounds for regarding
the goods as Japanese goods. Furthermore, you will realize that
in boycotting our matches, no single Japanese individual or con-
cern has come to harm. The boycott of our matches, therefore, is
not in agreement with the motive of the anti-Japanese boycott. If
the boycott is carried through against our matches, besides the
Swedish, American and British (Messrs. Boyd & Co.) interests, the
greatest sufferers will be the hundreds, if not thousands, of
Chinese shops having stocks of our matches, as well as the 600
laborers in the factory."

Mr. Liu's reply was, as nearly as I can recall:

"Since we now find definitely that the matches detained
in Chuanhow are Japanese, we first want to claim the $100,000
reward promised by you. Secondly, we suggest that you put the
blame for the sale of the Japanese matches in Fukien on Messrs.
Boyd & Co., whereby you will save your own interests. Messrs.
Boyd & Company's position in Fukien will thus be so much damaged
that they cannot carry on, and Messrs. Nam Chow & Co. will then
obtain your agency."

It is evident first of all that the individuals of the
committee, although they thoroughly realized my arguments, did not
wish to appear to have understood them, and also that the Committee
is definitely interested in obtaining the agency in Fukien for our
matches for Messrs. Nam Chow & Co. It is also clear from Mr. Liu's
statement that since he suggested that Messrs. Nam Chow & Co. take
the agency for our matches, that our matches will then no more
be Japanese from the moment that the agency is given to the Chinese
company instead of as now, to the British company. Consequently,
there is no motive whatever behind their attitude which can be
said to be based on anti-Japanese feelings. On the contrary, the
anti-Japanese boycott movement is here utilised for private and
personal interests.

As regards the reward of $100,000, I explained that I
had personally made a visit to the Temple of Heaven in the beginning
of 1932, when I was definitely told by the Anti-Japanese Boycott
Committee, then having their offices there, that they knew that our
matches were imported from Japan. As a result, we obtained cer-
tificates from the Swedish Consul-General for our Swedish imported
matches and the trade-marks belonging to the Swedish-Chinese Export
& Import Co. Ltd., as well as for our non-Swedish matches of the
Cathay Match Company's brands. We also obtained certificates
from the Consolidated Tax Administration of the Ministry of Finance
of the Chinese Government, all of which statements we printed on
pamphlets, stating at the side thereof our willingness to pay
$100,000 to anyone who could prove that we had imported any matches
under the above reproduced labels from Japan. No such imports
have, of course, been made.
page_data.zh:
投入燧松火柴公司（Sui Sung Match Co.）的资本，以及鉴于目前争议中的火柴使用瑞典商标，其生产由瑞典或美国资本资助，劳工完全为中国人，且原材料几乎全非日本产，因此不存在将货物视为日本货物的可接受理由。此外，您会意识到，在抵制我们的火柴过程中，没有任何单个日本人或日本商号受到损害。因此，抵制我们的火柴与反日抵制的动机不符。如果对我们的火柴实施抵制，除了瑞典、美国和英国（博伊德公司，Messrs. Boyd & Co.）的利益方外，受害最深的将是持有我们火柴库存的数百家乃至数千家中国商店，以及工厂内的600名工人。”

据我回忆，刘先生的答复大致如下：

“既然我们现在明确发现扣留在泉州（Chuanhow）的火柴是日本货，我们首先要求索取贵方承诺的10万美元赏金。其次，我们建议贵方将福建销售日本火柴的责任归咎于博伊德公司（Messrs. Boyd & Co.），以此保全贵方自身的利益。博伊德公司在福建的地位将因此受到严重损害而无法继续经营，届时南周公司（Messrs. Nam Chow & Co.）将获得贵方的代理权。”

首先显而易见的是，委员会的成员虽然完全理解我的论点，但不愿表现出他们已理解的样子；同时也明显看出，委员会确实有意为南周公司获取我们火柴在福建的代理权。从刘先生的陈述中也可以清楚地看出，既然他建议由南周公司代理我们的火柴，那么一旦代理权从现在的英国公司转交给这家中国公司，我们的火柴就不再是日本货了。因此，他们的态度背后没有任何可以说是基于反日情绪的动机。相反，这里的反日抵制运动被利用来谋取私人和个人的利益。

关于10万美元的赏金，我解释说，我在1932年初曾亲自前往天坛拜访，当时设在那里的反日抵制委员会明确告诉我，他们知道我们的火柴是从日本进口的。结果，我们就瑞典进口的火柴及属于瑞中出口有限公司（Swedish-Chinese Export & Import Co. Ltd.）的商标，以及国泰火柴公司（Cathay Match Company）品牌的非瑞典火柴，从瑞典总领事馆获得了证明书。我们还从中国国民政府财政部统税局获得了证明书，我们将所有这些声明印在小册子上，并在旁边注明我们愿意向任何能证明我们从日本进口了上述复刻标签下火柴的人支付10万美元。当然，此类进口从未发生过。

page_data.en:
-4-

In the course of the preceding conversation, Mr. Liu had
mentioned that at a meeting on the previous Saturday of the whole
Federation, a circular letter, allegedly sent out by our company,
had been read to the assembly in English and translated by an
English speaking Chinese into Chinese. The translation had been
verified by several other members of the Federation. Mr. Liu
stated that the Federation had been very angry on account of our
writing such a circular letter, which was supposed to be to the
effect that the boycott troubles in Fukien had been placed by us
in the hands of Mr. Eugene Kiang, barrister-at-law who was now
very optimistic and who had said that our difficulties could
easily be settled. It was clear that the members of the committee
had felt slighted by our discounting their power over us to such
an extent as shown by the circular letter.

The whole story of the circular letter is, however, a
fabrication, as no such circular letter has been written by us.
It is quite true that we have written, and probably stated, both
to Messrs. Boyd & Co. and to other interested individuals, that
the matter has been put in the hands of Mr. Kiang, the lawyer,
and that in our opinion the matter ought to be easily settled,
as we have completely clear papers and can prove to any individual
that there is not one copper or Japanese capital invested in the
manufacture of our matches.

Mr. Kiang asked me to step aside, spoke to me privately,
and said that he believed that the committee members were reluc-
tant to come out with their real interests in my presence. He
asked me to what extent we were prepared to spend money for the
settlement of the question, and suggested that he would speak to
the committee members privately after I had left.

I stated that I saw no reason in my prolonging my stay
and in prolonging the discussion of the matter, and that I therefore
wished to leave as soon as possible. Furthermore, that I was not
empowered to give any opinion as to the amount of capital that
could be spent by us to clear the trouble, and that Mr. Kiang,
as well as members of the committee, ought to be aware that the
matter was quite clearly understood by the committee members present.
It should, therefore, not be necessary to spend any further sums of
money. Mr. Kiang then intimated that he by his inquiry had meant
the fee payable to himself. I understood him to mean that, if the
fee is large enough, he could himself fix the committee members.
This, however, is only my opinion, and Mr. Kiang made no such direct
statement.

I then took leave of the various Chinese present, but was
again halted by Mr. Liu who, before I left, again made his statement
that they expected us to pay them $100,000. He also again suggested
that we agree to their burning the detained cargo in Chuancheow and
give the agency to Messrs. Ham Chow & Co. I asked Mr. Kiang to
reply for me to Mr. Liu, giving the same replies as I had already
given him on the same suggestion, whereafter I left. It was then
5 o'clock.
page_data.zh:
-4-

在前述谈话过程中，刘先生提到，在上个星期六的联合会全体会议上，宣读了一封据称由我公司发出的英文通函，并由一名懂英语的中国人翻译成中文。该译文经联合会的其他几名成员核实。刘先生表示，联合会因我们发出这样一封通函而非常愤怒，该通函的大意是福建的抵制麻烦已由我们交由尤金·蒋（Eugene Kiang）律师处理，蒋律师目前非常乐观，并称我们的困难可以轻易解决。显然，委员会成员感到受辱，因为通函显示我们如此轻视他们对我们的控制权。

然而，关于这封通函的整个故事纯属捏造，因为我们从未写过这样的通函。确有其事的是，我们确实曾写信给博伊德公司及其他相关人士，并可能曾表示，此事已交由蒋律师处理，且在我们看来，此事应能轻易解决，因为我们的文件完全清白，可以向任何人证明，在我们的火柴生产中没有任何一分一毫的日本资本投入。

蒋先生请我回避，私下对我说道，他认为委员会成员不愿在我面前透露他们的真实利益诉求。他询问我们准备花费多少钱来解决这个问题，并建议在我离开后，他将私下与委员会成员交谈。

我表示，我认为没有理由延长我的停留时间和对此事的讨论，因此我希望尽快离开。此外，我无权就我们可以花费多少资金来消除麻烦发表意见，蒋先生以及委员会成员应当清楚，在场的委员会成员对这件事已有十分清晰的理解。因此，没有必要再花费任何额外的款项。蒋先生随后暗示，他的询问是指应付给他本人的费用。我理解他的意思是，如果费用足够高，他就可以搞定委员会成员。然而，这只是我的意见，蒋先生并未做出如此直接的陈述。

随后我向在场的各位中国人告辞，但再次被刘先生拦住，他在我不离开前再次声明，他们期望我们支付给他们10万美元。他还再次建议我们同意他们在泉州（Chuancheow）焚烧被扣货物，并将代理权授予咸周公司（Messrs. Ham Chow & Co.）。我请蒋先生代我回复刘先生，给予我之前针对同一建议已给出的相同答复，随后我便离开了。当时是5点钟。

1st September, 1932.

General T. . . u,
Mayor of Greater Shanghai,
SHANGHAI.

Sir,

Boycott activities against our Matches.

We have followed with great interest your very admirable efforts to check the illegal activities of the various groups of boycotters which were threatening the peace of this City.

Especially gratifying was the report in this morning's newspapers of your Manifesto issued to the Public yesterday.

We trust, that you will now see your way to stop the illegal activities against our firms and our matches. We refer in this respect to our letter addressed to you on the 24th of last month. Over 5,000 packages of our matches are still detained by the boycotters in Chuanchiu. The original cause of the detention was a telegram dispatched by the Shanghai National Salvation Federation. We have met the representatives of this group: Messrs. Chilling Yin (殷芝齡) and P. S. G. Lieu (劉士庚). We have, through our Chinese lawyer Mr. Eugene Y. B. Yang demonstrated to these gentlemen absolute and definite proof of non-existence of Japanese interests in our matches. The American, British and Swedish Consular Authorities have given their assurance to the same effect. In spite of this Messrs. Chilling Yin and S. Y. Lieu are adamant and refuse to cable to Chuanchiu to release the goods. No patriotic reasons can be behind their refusal.

Our Chuanchiu agents have telegraphed us, that the local Boycott Committee has threatened to have our matches publicly burned on the 4th of September.

Under the circumstances we should be exceedingly obliged to you if you would instruct the parties responsible in Shanghai to send a telegram to Chuanchiu to the effect that the goods be immediately released thereby undoing the evil caused by their first telegram to that port. Our Chinese friends in Chuanchiu have requested that we ask the Shanghai

1932年9月1日。

致 T. . . u 将军，
大上海市长，
上海。

先生：

针对我方火柴的抵制活动。

我们要以极大的兴趣关注您为遏制威胁本市和平的各派抵制者非法活动所做出的令人钦佩的努力。

尤其令人欣慰的是，今早报纸报道了您昨日向公众发布的宣言。

我们相信，您现在会设法停止针对我司及我方火柴的非法活动。在此方面，我们提及上月24日致您的信函。我们在泉州（Chuanchiu）仍有5,000多包火柴被抵制者扣留。扣留的最初原因是上海全国救国联合会发出的一份电报。我们会见了该团体的代表：殷芝龄（Chilling Yin）先生和刘士庚（P. S. G. Lieu）先生。我们通过我们的中国律师杨 Eugene Y. B. 先生向这些绅士展示了绝对且确凿的证据，证明我们的火柴中不存在日本利益。美国、英国和瑞典领事当局也给予了同样的保证。尽管如此，殷芝龄先生和刘士庚先生仍固执己见，拒绝发电报至泉州放行货物。他们的拒绝背后没有任何爱国理由。

我们在泉州的代理人致电我们称，当地抵制委员会威胁要在9月4日公开焚烧我们的火柴。

在这种情况下，如果您能指示上海有关方面向泉州发送一份电报，要求立即放行货物，从而消除其第一份电报对该港口造成的恶劣影响，我们将不胜感激。我们在泉州的中国朋友请求我们请上海

authorities to get in touch with General Mao Yee Siao
( 毛 义 孝 ), 61st Division of the 19th Route Army, now at Chuanchiu.
This letter will be sent to you through the courtesy of
the Swedish Consulate-General.

Yours faithfully,

JW/TV

27th August, 1935.

J. . H. Mckhoff, Esq.,
Charge d'Affaires,
The Danish Legation,
PEKING.

Sir,

The Swedish Legation's Protest against Boycott activities against
Swedish matches.

We have the honour to confirm the exchange of tele-
grams as per enclosed copies (4).

We received early yesterday telegram in information
from Messrs. Boyd & Co. in Fukien that further 300 cases "Lucky
Boy" and 300 cartons "Temple" matches (cases and cartons of same
contents) had been detained at Chuanchiu in the Soon Seng ware-
house and that the date for burning of the cargo had been set
at September the 4th.

We added in our cable report to you that the time of
manufacture of the cargo was the spring this year. The reason
for this information is evident from the contents of our letter
of the 25th August to you, as it demonstrates that the matches
have been made several months after the American company purchased
the factory at Shanghai. Needless to say, the American company
has no connections whatever with the earlier organization, and
has taken steps to eliminate from the factory anything and every-
thing of Japanese character so as to avoid any complications due
to the boycott. Thus, even Japanese scales and instruments,
Japanese books and, of course, all Japanese employees were
immediately dispensed with. We hardly believe that we need make
any further explanations above what was said in our letter of the
25th August. Perhaps only the position between the Swedish and
the American company might be clarified.

Of the 2,500 shares of the American company 2,492 are
held by the International Match Corporation of New York in trust
for the Swedish Match Co. The International Match Corporation
page_data.zh:
7
1935年8月27日。

致 J. . H. Mckhoff 先生，
代办，
丹麦公使馆，
北平。

先生：

瑞典公使馆就针对瑞典火柴的抵制活动提出的抗议。

我们荣幸地确认随附副本（4）所示的电报交换情况。

昨天一早，我们收到福建博伊德公司（Messrs. Boyd & Co.）发来的电报通知，另有300箱“幸运男孩”（Lucky Boy）牌火柴和300纸箱“庙宇”（Temple）牌火柴（箱和纸箱内装物相同）在泉州的顺生（Soon Seng）仓库被扣留，且定下的焚货日期为9月4日。

我们在发给您的电报报告中补充说明，该批货物的生产时间为今年春季。提供这一信息的原因在您8月25日致我们的信函内容中显而易见，因为它表明这些火柴是在美国公司购买上海工厂数月后生产的。毋庸赘言，美国公司与之前的组织没有任何关联，并已采取措施清除工厂内所有具有日本性质的事物，以避免因抵制而产生任何纠纷。因此，即使是日本的秤和仪器、日本书籍，当然还有所有日本雇员，都立即被遣散。我们认为，除了8月25日信函中所述内容外，几乎不需要再做进一步解释。或许只需澄清一下瑞典公司与美国公司之间的关系。

在美国公司的2,500股股份中，有2,492股由纽约国际火柴公司（International Match Corporation）为瑞典火柴公司（Swedish Match Co.）信托持有。国际火柴公司

page_data.en:
- 2 -

in its turn is, as you are most likely aware, subordinate to the
Swedish Match Co. Although the factory definitely belongs to
the American company incorporated at Washington, duly registered
with the American authorities, the Swedish Match Co. is directly
interested in the manufacture.

The manufacture, besides, is to the greater extent
made under the Cathay Match Co.'s Swedish owned trade marks under
orders placed with the American company by the Swedish company.

The American company is a manufacturing company only
and the sales agency for their matches has been given to the
Cathay Match Co. Upon delivery of matches from the factory on
the Swedish Co.'s orders the matches cease to be American
property and become Swedish property, whether matches under
American or Swedish trade marks are concerned.

The former shipment of 1,590 packages "Chao" matches
was American property until shipped and Swedish property until
paid on the 20th instant when it became British property. The
latter quantity of 300 packages once "Lucky Boy" and "Temple"
is still Swedish property. This shipment is a consignment ship-
ment and will, consequently, not be paid for until delivered
and disposed of.

The above ought to clarify any questions in which you
might possibly be interested, and which have not already been
explained.

As to the boycott activities we know that both the
Chinese Chamber of Commerce in Shanghai and the so-called
National Salvation Federation in Shanghai have been parties in
engineering the boycott against us. We know that the Chinese
match interests are well represented in the Chinese Chamber but
we can, of course, not make any accusations on this ground. We
can say, however, that the Chinese Chamber has definitely re-
fused us assistance on application by both the American Consulate
and the American Chamber of Commerce as well as the Swedish
Chamber of Commerce.

It has also been reported to us that the Chinese
match companies, represented in the National Salvation Federa-
tion, are "greatly interested" in the outcome of the present
case.

As for the boycotters' attitude toward us you will
get an idea of the position if you take part of the enclosed
memorandum written by a member of this company as minutes of a
meeting on the 17th inst. where he was present.

The Boycott Federation in Shanghai is very well aware
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

正如贵方极有可能知晓的那样，该公司本身隶属于瑞典火柴公司（Swedish Match Co.）。尽管该工厂明确属于在华盛顿注册、并经美国当局正式登记的美国公司，但瑞典火柴公司对制造业务拥有直接利益。

此外，大部分生产活动是根据瑞典公司向美国公司下达的订单，使用华夏火柴公司（Cathay Match Co.）旗下瑞典所有的商标进行的。

该美国公司仅是一家制造公司，其火柴的销售代理权已授予华夏火柴公司。一旦根据瑞典公司的订单从工厂交付火柴，无论涉及的是美国商标还是瑞典商标，这些火柴便不再属于美国财产，而转为瑞典财产。

此前装运的1,590包“朝”牌火柴在装运前属于美国财产，在运输途中属于瑞典财产，直至本月20日付款后转为英国财产。后一批300包曾名为“幸运男孩”（Lucky Boy）和“庙”（Temple）牌的火柴目前仍属瑞典财产。这批货物是寄售货物，因此只有在交付并售出后才需付款。

上述内容应能澄清贵方可能感兴趣且尚未得到解释的任何疑问。

关于抵制活动，我们知道上海总商会和所谓的上海全国救国联合会都参与了策划针对我们的抵制行动。我们知道中国火柴业利益方在上海总商会中有着充分的代表，但我们当然不能以此为由提出任何指控。然而，我们可以说，在美国领事馆、美国商会以及瑞典商会提出申请时，上海总商会明确拒绝向我们提供协助。

另据向我们报告，在全国救国联合会中有代表的中国火柴公司对当前案件的结果“极为关注”。

至于抵制者对我们的态度，如果贵方查阅随函附上的由本公司一名成员作为会议纪要所写的备忘录（他出席了本月17日的会议），便可对局势有所了解。

上海抵制联合会非常清楚

page_data.en:
- 3 -

that the activities against us and our matches are absolutely
unfounded. As you will see from the enclosed minutes it is
apparent that the motives for the boycott lie in personal greed
as well as in interests to favour Chinese friends of the boycotters
versus in particular our present British agents in the Fukien
Province.

As regards the claim of $100,000, the boycotters'
basing this claim on our reward certificate is a mere bluff.
We enclose a reward certificate herewith from which you will see
that we have promised $100,000 reward to anyone who can prove
that we have imported matches under the brands in question,
shown on the certificate, from Japan. No such imports have,
of course, been made. The reward certificate was published in
the main Chinese papers in Shanghai as a result of claims made
by the former Anti-Japanese Boycott Society that our matches
were of Japanese import. Hence the wording.

The claim for $100,000 has, of course, not been made
in writing. As a matter of fact we hold no documents in writing
from the National Salvation Federation. They are evidently
careful not to commit themselves in black and white and have not
replied to letters addressed to them.

Their verbal request for $100,000 has also been made
direct to representatives of Messrs. Boyd & Co. who have been
told that in case the money is paid there will be no further
trouble, but in case of such troubles the Shanghai Boycott
Federation would assist, most likely such assistance again to
be economically supported by us. It is evident that the
boycott is here being made use of for a blackmail racket.

The boycotters in Chuanchin allege to have found out-
side the packages of the detained "Wheel" cargo chops including
the Sui Sung characters. Their statement is quite possible as
the American company took over some ready stocks under the Cathay
Match Co.'s brands made during the last months of 1931. It can
also be explained from the fact that the tax office representative
at the factory used an old chop containing the Sui Sung characters
until the 4th of March, although the American company took over
the factory as from the 1st of January. We enclose a translation
of a letter received from the Consolidated Tax Bureau in expla-
nation hereof. As will be seen from the letter in question the
Tax Bureau claims that all shipments to Fukien have been 1932
manufacture. Nevertheless, we admit that it is quite possible
that some matches of late 1931 manufacture might have been
shipped. This should make no different, however, as in either
case they are equally much definitely not Japanese, and as in
either case they were American property until purchased by us
from the American company, when they became Swedish.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

针对我们及我们火柴的活动是毫无根据的。正如贵方从所附会议纪要中所见，抵制的动机显然在于个人贪婪，以及偏向抵制者的中国朋友（特别是相对于我们目前在福建省的英国代理商）的利益。

关于10万美元的索赔要求，抵制者以我们的悬赏证书为依据提出此索赔纯属虚张声势。随函附上一份悬赏证书，从中可见，我们承诺向任何能证明我们从日本进口了证书上所示相关品牌火柴的人支付10万美元奖金。当然，并未发生此类进口行为。该悬赏证书是在前抗日救国会声称我们的火柴为日本进口品并提出指控后，刊登在上海主要中文报纸上的。因此才有了这样的措辞。

当然，这10万美元的索赔要求并未以书面形式提出。事实上，我们未持有来自全国救国联合会的任何书面文件。他们显然小心翼翼地避免留下白纸黑字的承诺，并且未回复致他们的信件。

他们口头提出的10万美元要求也是直接向博伊德公司（Messrs. Boyd & Co.）的代表提出的，并被告知如果支付这笔钱，就不会再有麻烦；但如果出现此类麻烦，上海抵制联合会将提供协助，而这种协助很可能再次由我们在经济上支持。显然，这里的抵制正被用作一种敲诈勒索的手段。

泉州的抵制者声称在被扣押的“轮”牌货物包装外发现了包括“瑞松”字样的印章。他们的说法是完全可能的，因为这家美国公司在1931年最后几个月接管了华夏火柴公司品牌下的一些现成库存。这也可能是因为尽管美国公司自1月1日起接管了工厂，但工厂的税务局代表直到3月4日仍在使用一枚带有“瑞松”字样的旧印章。随函附上从统税局收到的一封信的译文，对此进行了解释。从该信可以看出，统税局声称所有运往福建的货物均为1932年制造。尽管如此，我们承认完全有可能部分1931年末制造的火柴已被装运。然而，这不应造成任何差异，因为无论哪种情况，它们都同样明确不是日本产品；而且无论哪种情况，在我们从美国公司购买之前，它们都是美国财产，购买后才转为瑞典财产。

page_data.en:
- 4 -

In the moment of writing this we received a report
from the Clarke's Inquiry Agency, of which a copy is enclosed.
They had been engaged by us to be present at the boycott meet-
ing. We have also had a Chinese lawyer on the spot from whom we
have not yet received a report. Messrs. Boyd & Co. have also
got representatives working for their side in the boycott group.

As regards the mayor's order to Chuanchiu for the
natives to be released we have reason to doubt that the Chuanchiu
boycotters will take any notice thereof. It will be noted that
the mayor definitely prohibited the boycott meeting on the 26th.
It was held, nevertheless, and is to continue both today the
27th and tomorrow.

Since the activities originate from the Shanghai
Federation we therefore suggested in our cable that you request
the mayor to bear pressure upon that body in Shanghai. It is
our opinion that the Fukien societies are here being made use
of by the big boycott heads in Shanghai for their personal
interests.

The American-Consulate-General has cabled to the
American Legation. We do not know what action has been taken.
The American Consul General also yesterday personally sought
an interview with General Tsai Ding Kai, the head of the 19th
Route Army. The General is at present in Shanghai while the
19th Route Army is in Fukien with headquarters at Chuanchiu.
We are not however aware whether a meeting was arranged nor, if so,
of any results.

We shall take care to keep you posted of any future
developments and have the honour to express our sincere thanks
for the very valuable assistance rendered already.

We remain,

Sir,

Yours faithfully,

Enc.
TAH/TV
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

在撰写本文时，我们收到了克拉克调查社（Clarke's Inquiry Agency）的一份报告，副本随函附上。我们曾聘请他们出席抵制会议。我们还有一位中国律师在现场，但我们尚未收到他的报告。博伊德公司也有代表在抵制团体中为他们一方工作。

关于市长下令泉州释放当地人的命令，我们有理由怀疑泉州抵制者是否会予以理会。值得注意的是，市长明确禁止了在26日举行的抵制会议。然而，会议仍然举行，并将在今天27日和明天继续举行。

由于这些活动源于上海联合会，因此我们在电报中建议，请贵方要求市长对上海的该机构施加压力。我们认为，福建的各社团正被上海的大型抵制头目利用，以谋取其个人利益。

美国总领事馆已致电美国公使馆。我们不知道采取了什么行动。美国总领事昨天还亲自寻求会见第十九路军军长蔡廷锴将军。蔡将军目前在上海，而第十九路军在福建，总部设在泉州。然而，我们不知是否安排了会晤，也不知如有会晤，结果如何。

我们将随时向贵方通报任何后续进展，并对贵方迄今提供的宝贵协助表示诚挚感谢。

此致，

先生，

您忠实的，

附件
TAH/TV

30th March, 193 .

J. . . . Ickhoff, Esq.,
Charge d'Affaires,
The British Legation,
Peking.

Sir,

The Swedish Legation's Protest against Boycott activities.

We have for acknowledgement your letters of the 25th
and 26th inst.

The situation is at present unchanged except as regards
a report that union boycott representatives, whom we have seen
in person, have sent "favourable" tel. grs to Amoy and Chuan-
chiu.

As regards protests made to the British Consul; we do
not think that the British Legation will receive any reports at
this time. The American as well as the Swedish Consulates-Gene-
ral have given us unrestricted and open handed assistance in
every way possible. Messrs. Boyd & Co. who applied for assistance
from the British Consulate-General in Shanghai for protection of
their property received an entirely different treatment. The
view point of the British Consulate-General at Shanghai is that
only if Messrs. Boyd & Co. can complain that the Amoy Consulate
has mishandled the case, would they take up the matter from Shang-
hai.

Both the British and American Consulates in Fukien have
done everything in their power and may be said to have brought
about the release of other quantities detained in several other
places in Fukien.

In this connection we notice from your letter of the
2 th inst. that the American Legation understands the present
protest to be made regarding the same goods of which they have
long ago received information. That is not so. Matches were
detained in June in Chuanchiu and were later released due to the
action of the American Consulate at Amoy. Protests were, of
course, made by us to the American Consulate-General who
instructed their Amoy Consulate to deal with the case in
which they were then successful. We therefore dealt with the

193 . 年3月30日

J. . . . Ickhoff 先生，
代办，
英国公使馆，
北平。

先生，

瑞典公使馆关于抵制活动的抗议。

贵方本月25日和26日的来信已收悉。

目前的局势除了一份报告外没有变化，该报告称我们亲眼见过的工会抵制代表已向厦门和泉州发送了“有利”的电报。

关于向英国领事提出的抗议；我们认为英国公使馆此时不会收到任何报告。美国总领事馆和瑞典总领事馆已在各方面向我们提供了不受限制且慷慨的协助。博伊德公司为保护其财产向上海英国总领事馆申请协助，却得到了截然不同的对待。上海英国总领事馆的观点是，只有当博伊德公司投诉厦门领事馆处理案件不当时，他们才会从上海介入此事。

福建的英国和美国领事馆均已竭尽全力，可以说促成了在福建其他几个地方被扣押的其他批次货物的释放。

在此方面，我们从贵方本月2日来信中注意到，美国公使馆理解当前的抗议是针对他们早已获悉的同一批货物。事实并非如此。火柴于6月在泉州被扣押，后因美国驻厦门领事馆的行动而被释放。当然，我们向美国总领事馆提出了抗议，总领事馆指示其厦门领事馆处理此案，并取得了成功。因此，我们就

page_data.en:
- 2 -

Amoy Consulate direct with regard to this new case in Chuan chin
and only after the Amoy Consulate has definitely failed to bring
about the release of the goods were any protests made to the
Consulate-General at Shanghai.

We hope that we shall be able to send you information
with our next mail that the goods have been released. We can
hardly believe it possible that, in face of the protests made
by the Swedish, British and American Authorities, as well as of
ourselves, the Chinese authorities will not take action.

We have the honor to remain,

Sir,

Yours faithfully,

TAH/TG
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

这一发生在泉州的新案件直接与厦门领事馆交涉，只有在厦门领事馆明确未能促成货物释放后，才向上海总领事馆提出抗议。

我们希望能在下一班邮件中向贵方发送货物已获释的信息。我们很难相信，面对瑞典、英国和美国当局以及我们自身的抗议，中国当局会不采取行动。

此致，

先生，

您忠实的，

TAH/TG

25th August, 1935.

J. V. P. Mc'eehin, Esq.,
Chairman The General Chamber of Commerce, Shanghai,
c/o Messrs. Ilbert & Co.,
1, Canton Road,
SHANGHAI.

Dear Sir,

Match Boycott.

Confirming our telephone conversation with you yesterday evening we beg to express our thanks for the kind attitude taken by you and enclose herewith a draft in English and Chinese of a letter for the Chinese Chamber of Commerce. Regarding this draft we wish to make the following explanations.

First paragraph. The shipments concerns 1,500 cartons of 100 dozen boxes each "Wheel" matches. The trade mark belongs to the Cathay Match Co., Ltd. The matches have been purchased by us from the American-Far Eastern Match Co. Federal Inc. U.S.A. and sold to Messrs. Boyd & Co. As will be seen from the letter heading of this paper we represent the Cathay Match Co. The letter may be explained to be merely the name under which this company is trading in China with matches of non Swedish origin.

Second paragraph. The information regarding a telegram received in Chuanchiu from the National Salvation Federation in Shanghai we have from the Chuanchiu Chinese press. As regards the telegram sent by the Chinese Chamber of Commerce it was addressed to the Anti-Japanese Boycott Association in Kingkiang, Fukien, same as Chuanchiu, where the matches are now detained. The telegram was sent about the middle of June. It was despatched immediately after a call made at the Chinese Chamber of the following gentleman: Consul Maher representing the American Consulate-General, Mr. H. M. Gibb, secretary of the American Chamber of Commerce, Mr. J. W. Wulfsberg representing the Swedish companies, Mr. H. J. Rehn representing the American company and Mr. T. Hultman.

At this meeting absolute definite proof was demonstrated by the American Consulate and Chamber representatives of the non-Japanese origin of the matches. The representatives of the
